children: Indian IT stocks could see further gains in the near term after Accenture's latest results and guidance offered some comfort on the global technology spending environment, according to Dharmesh Kant, Head of Research at Chola Securities.

Kant said the recent rally in IT stocks was more tactical in nature, but believes select large-cap names could still deliver further upside. He expects Indian IT companies to post broadly similar trends to Accenture, with currency depreciation providing some support to earnings.

“Indian IT companies will report similar kind of numbers this time around, with a one-year forward outlook and with currency depreciation setting to play reported INR numbers will be around 10 to 12%. So that definitely gives a floor and hope trade to play out for the Indian IT companies, and they have corrected quite a lot.”

Among the IT names, Kant favours Tata Consultancy Services, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra, with an estimated upside of around 5-7% from current levels and the potential to stretch towards 10% from a tactical trading perspective.
Bank of India stands out among lenders
In the banking space, Kant is positive on Bank of India, citing strong deposit and credit growth along with attractive valuations.
The bank reported deposit growth of 21.6%, while credit growth stood at 20.4%. The RAM segment — retail, agriculture and MSME — also grew 18.57%, according to Kant.

He noted that Bank of India is trading at less than 0.69 times one-year forward price-to-book, making its valuation attractive compared with other banking names. He also expects the Reserve Bank of India to potentially pause its rate action in the near term, which could support banking stocks.
Kant expects net interest margins (NIMs) across banks to improve by around 20 basis points as the benefit of the gap between borrowing costs and deposit costs feeds through.
"Bank of India is the top pick for today's morning," Kant said, adding that the stock was his preferred banking pick from a medium-term perspective.
Tata Motors preferred in auto space
Kant remains constructive on the auto sector despite the weakness seen in some passenger vehicle stocks after the latest monthly sales data.

He believes the base effect could become more pronounced in October, while higher input costs could put pressure on margins. However, commercial vehicles stood out, with strong volume growth reported by Tata Motors.

Tata Motors' commercial vehicle volumes grew around 42%, while Ashok Leyland also posted strong growth, according to Kant. He expects this momentum to support earnings and offset some margin pressure.
Kant pointed to Tata Motors' valuation at around 20 times earnings, along with an expected return on equity of more than 30%, as factors supporting the stock.
Cautious on cement stocks
Kant is less positive on the cement sector despite expectations of price hikes and a recovery in demand after the monsoon.

Cement companies have already raised prices by around ₹7-10 per bag, with further hikes expected in the third and fourth quarters. However, higher input costs could offset much of the benefit from these price increases.

While volumes could grow by around 9-10%, Kant expects limited improvement in EBITDA per tonne. Within the sector, he prefers UltraTech Cement among largecaps and Dalmia Bharat for its presence in the eastern market, but sees both as trading opportunities rather than structural long-term bets.
Kant continues to favour Coal India, particularly as e-auction volumes gain traction. He highlighted better realisations from e-auction sales, especially in the northern region.
At around ₹420-425, Kant sees Coal India moving towards ₹450-460. He also pointed to the company's dividend yield of around 6% as an additional attraction.
However, he sees the stock more as a trading opportunity rather than a long-term wealth-creation bet.

title: IT, banks, autos: Dharmesh Kant shares top stock picks and sector outlook
